newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seeks to bring PMDB into re-election fold.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seeks to bring PMDB into re-election fold.

text.p: The Brazilian government on Wednesday was seeking ways of persuading its largest ally in Congress to take part in a latest scheduled vote on re-election, officials said.

Opposition within the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) forced the government on Tuesday to postpone until next week a first vote in the Chamber of Deputies on a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election.
The vote had been scheduled for today and the delay gave the government more time to persuade the PMDB, the biggest in Congress, to take part in the vote.

The PMDB is split on whether its lawmakers can ignore a recommendation by a party convention not to vote on re-election until February 15, after elections to choose the new presidents of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate due February 4.
"We're going full steam ahead and now the PMDB has to decide whether it's with us or against us," said a spokeswoman for the government's chief whip in the Chamber of Deputies, Benito Gama.

Government whips told the PMDB's leader in the lower house, Dep. Michel Temer, they would withdraw their support for his candidacy as president of the Chamber of Deputies if the party continued to dither over re-election, the spokeswoman said.
The government was also seeking to counter resistance in the Senate to its plan to vote on re-election in the Chamber of Deputies next week.

PMDB senator Ronaldo Cunha Lima was personally assured by President Cardoso on Tuesday the government would not seek to undermine the party's candidate for Senate president, Sen. Iris Rezende, an aide to Cunha Lima said.

Fears the government might work behind the scenes in favor of the Liberal Front Party's candidate in the Senate, political boss Sen. Antonio Carlos Magalhaes, prompted the PMDB to recommend its members not to vote on re-election until February 15.

"The senator is meeting with other senators, but there is no agreement so far," said the aide, adding that Cunha Lima himself remained in favor of voting on re-election only after congressional elections due February 4.
